A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CMT-Benchmark and contain complete, readable main text, tables, figures, equations, references, and Appendix A. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable matching across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 models on 50 problems in Section 4, Table 2, and Figure 3, plus model-output case studies in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original 17-model benchmark results and all four model-output case studies in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The problem-construction workflow, symbolic parser, non-commutative operator handling, and final-answer grading procedure are unchanged. Section 3.1.1 expands the explanation of discarding intermediate reasoning without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 50 problems across seven computational/theoretical categories plus Other, using the same four answer modalities. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 contains the same 17 evaluated models, and Appendix A retains the same four models in its case studies. The newly cited scientific benchmarks do not become evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both versions retain evaluation on all 50 problems, Pass@1, final boxed-answer equivalence checks, and human grading for some parsing failures. v2 newly describes the existing evaluation as zero-shot, closed-book, and without domain-specific fine-tuning; it does not revise a previously stated setting or report a new protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A preserves all four case studies: triangular-lattice charge ordering, symmetry-sector counting, fluctuation-dissipation, and Fermi-surface topology. Their model excerpts and failure diagnoses are unchanged, with no added ablations or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain the same 11.4±2.1% cross-model summary and uncertainty presentation. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Every model-by-topic score in Table 2 is unchanged, including GPT-5 at 30%, GPT-o3 at 26%, and GPT-5-mini at 24%. Figure 3, the counts of 18 universally unsolved problems and 26 solved by at most one model, and the appendix findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The problem equations, operator-algebra reasoning, and mathematical discussions in Appendix A are unchanged. No formal assumptions, definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about an expert-authored research-level benchmark, automated grading, and gaps in current models' scientific reasoning. Abstract edits do not materially change these claims or their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly qualifies the intended evaluation scope as out-of-the-box, zero-shot, closed-book performance without domain-specific fine-tuning. Section 3.1.1 also explains the focus on final research conclusions; the substantive failure-mode interpretations in the conclusion and appendix remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents zero-shot, closed-book evaluation without domain-specific fine-tuning, improving the description of the existing experiments. The dataset access reference and promise of a future grading-code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and bibliography add PHYSICS, CURIE, Pan et al.'s quantum many-body calculations work, and SPIQA. This modestly expands scientific-AI context; the existing related-work comparisons and novelty positioning are retained.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, expands the final-answer evaluation explanation, adds an evaluation-goal sentence and funding acknowledgments, and updates bibliography formatting. The section organization and most prose, including Appendix A, remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 9 to page 10, and appendix example boxes and surrounding text are repaginated. The figures, table structures, captions, and plotted content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves transparency by explicitly stating the evaluation conditions and explaining its final-answer focus. Four additional citations improve research context. These gains are limited: the benchmark, empirical evidence, and substantive case-study analyses remain unchanged.
